conflict_topics: Noise / music during evenings (Agent B's night shift sleep)
Tent location vs. morning exercise group (shade / shared use of space)
dialogue_quality_notes: Polite, context-appropriate condolences framed the negotiations and made concessions easier ('sorry for your loss').
Participants gave concrete reasons for their requests (wheelchair access, night shift sleep, morning exercise group and shade) which grounded the negotiation.
Resolutions are explicit and recorded in speech (D's concession on music and offer to move the tent; C's withdrawal).
evaluation.final_reason: The parties made concrete, mutual agreements by speech: Agent D agreed to shift the tent so the path would allow wheelchair access ('We can shift it, no problem. Will it be okay if we move it more to the side here?'), Agent C withdrew the claim and said they would find another shaded spot ('I'll have to find another spot.'), and Agent D conceded on the music after negotiation ('Alright, no music from 7 to 10 tonight and Sunday.'). These spoken acceptances resolved the outstanding substantive conflicts.
position_change_notes: Agent D changed position on music: initially offered to keep music very soft (compromise), then conceded to no music 7–10 ('Alright, no music from 7 to 10 tonight and Sunday.').
Agent C relinquished the claim to that specific morning spot and agreed to seek alternatives ('I'll have to find another spot.').
Agent A acted as a mediator/suggester (proposed pavilion) and did not change a strong opposing stance.
Agent B persisted in requesting no music for sleep but accepted the spoken settlement once D agreed.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: '...it's blocking the path to the lift. My mother needs to get through with her wheelchair.' Agent D: '...We can shift it, no problem. Will it be okay if we move it more to the side here?' (new, substantive disagreement about walkway/access; D offers to move but A has not yet accepted)

Agent A accepted the move: 'Yes, thank you. As long as there's enough space for a wheelchair to get through, that's fine.' New, separate issue raised: Agent B: '...I'm worried about the noise.' (wheelchair issue moving toward resolution; noise concern newly introduced and unresolved)

Agent D: '...We'll be mindful and keep the volume down.' Agent B: 'Would it be possible to not have the music on, maybe from 7 p.m. to 10 p.m.? ... it's just for tonight and Sunday.' (negotiation on noise; D softened but B makes a firmer request—still unresolved)

Agent C: '...my morning exercise group uses this spot every day at 7 a.m.' Agent D: '...this is my grandfather's wake. The tent will be here until Monday. We can't move it every morning.' (clear, substantive spatial-use conflict; D states refusal)

Agent C: 'The only thing is, the other open area by the playground has no shade.' Later: 'Okay, I understand. I'll have to find another spot. Does anyone happen to know another place with some shade in the morning?' (C effectively concedes/withdraws the claim about that spot; however the unresolved noise issue from B remains)
Agent D addresses music: '...What if we keep it on, but very, very soft from 7 to 10? So it won't disturb you.' (D offers a compromise — reduces but does not settle B's request for no music)

Agent B: 'Is it possible we could stick to the original idea, no music just from 7 p.m. to 10 p.m.? ... only for tonight and Sunday.' Agent D: 'Alright, no music from 7 to 10 tonight and Sunday.' (explicit mutual agreement; D concedes music for the requested times — last substantive conflict settled)
Agent C asks for shaded alternatives and Agent A suggests: 'What about the pavilion over by the next block? It gets some shade in the morning.' (planning, no conflict)
Agent C: 'Oh, the pavilion. That's a good idea. Thanks, Agent A. I'll check it out.' Agent B thanks Agent D. (no substantive disagreement)
Agent D: 'It's okay, Agent B.' (closure / reassurance; no conflict)

substantive_insights: Conflicts were practical and schedule-based (accessibility, sleep schedule, regular exercise spot) rather than identity or value clashes.
Agent D balanced emotional needs (music important at a wake) against neighbors' practical needs and ultimately made a concession on music while proposing a softer alternative first.
Resolution used different mechanisms: accommodation (tent shift), concession (no music 7–10), and withdrawal (C agreeing to find another spot).
